accuracy.title: Accuracy
accuracy.heading: How well Painfold finds personal data
accuracy.lead: Out of 100 names in your feedback, Painfold removes about {n}. That's why you review every finding before sharing.

findings.names: Names: {removal} are removed in German and English feedback, and at least {min} in every one of {groups} name-origin groups.
findings.rules: Emails, phone numbers, IBANs and the other kinds of personal data: {removal} of the values in hand-written hard cases are removed.
findings.targetMet: Stage 2 target, at least {target} of names removed in every group: met.
findings.targetMissed: Stage 2 target, at least {target} of names removed in every group: not met yet.

measured.heading: How it's measured
measured.sets: Painfold is measured on made-up feedback with known personal data, in German and English: hand-written hard cases, hand-written names typical of 13 communities living in Austria, long texts, and generated messages.
measured.browser: The name model is measured in a browser, the way it runs for you. Its rules were tuned on a separate set of sentences; the test sentences were checked only once, after tuning. They were written by the same person who tuned the rules, so a test set written by someone else is planned.
measured.terms: Removed: the value is gone from the cleaned file, whatever kind of data it was taken for. Removed as a name: removed and recognised as a name.

names.heading: Names
names.list: {onList} of {total} test names contain a first name from Painfold's list. The list is used only right after a greeting, a thank-you, a sign-off or an introduction ("hi anna", "LG Markus").

groups.heading: By name-origin group
groups.note: The groups exist only in the test data, so that names from every community are measured. Painfold never infers anyone's origin.
groups.perLanguage: Per language, each group has only 12 or 13 test names, so one miss moves it by about 8 points. The target applies to each group across both languages.
groups.detail: As a name {typeCorrect}, without the list {withoutList}

long.heading: Names in long texts
long.note: The name model reads about 300 words at a time, so longer texts are checked in overlapping parts. These texts are four to five times that long.

rules.heading: Other personal data
rules.note: Hand-written hard cases: values written in unusual ways, pasted or disguised, and look-alikes that must not be removed, such as order numbers.
rules.explain: Found: the share of values removed as the right kind of data. Correct: the share of findings that really were that kind of data.
rules.generated: Generated data (a check that nothing broke)
rules.generatedNote: Messages built from the same templates as the sample file. The detectors could be tuned to these sentences, so the numbers are high by design: they show that nothing broke.

gaps.heading: Known gaps
items: English names in English sentences are the weakest area: 11 of 13 are removed. That is too few names to judge one language on its own; a larger test set is planned (#82).
Nicknames after a greeting or thank-you that are not on the first-name list, such as "cheers ollie".
Names at the start of a sentence, with nothing before them: "Sanne van der Berg says…".
Some particles and multi-part names: "Saif ur Rehman", "Tesfaye Bekele".
Small towns: in "Mehmet Aydın aus Wels" the name is removed, but not "Wels".
Email addresses spelled out to fool spam filters ("name AT example DOT net").
English addresses that start with a flat number ("Flat 2, 14 Market Street").
A few document numbers that look like an Austrian social security number are removed although they are not one.
gaps.mark: Anything missed can be marked in the review with M.

speed.heading: Speed
speed.text: A file with 5,000 rows is checked for emails, phone numbers and the other rule-based data in about 1.5 seconds. With the name model in your browser, names in it take 70 to 115 seconds, checked in the background while you review.

model.heading: The name model
model.text: Names and places are found by {model} ({license}), a multilingual model trained on news text, including the CoNLL-2003 data set. The CoNLL texts are themselves licensed, which is a grey area for models trained on them. Painfold serves the model from its own site and runs it in your browser.

warnings.heading: Could identify someone
warnings.text: Painfold warns about text that can point to one person together with other details: exact ages, “the only …”, job titles with a small place, and roles one person holds. Warnings are never removed on their own. Measured on {n} hand-written warnings, with the places given; the set is small and was written by the same author as the rules, so expect real feedback to score lower.
